entries.what_happened: Two OpenAI manuscripts in the openai/math release claim the sharp logarithmic exponent of off-diagonal classical Ramsey numbers r(s,t) (the two-colour numbers R(s,t) in the problem's notation; r(s,t) is the least n such that every graph on n vertices has a K_s or an independent t-set). (1) 'The Sharp Logarithmic Exponent of r(5,t)' (paper.tex, dated 24 September 2026) claims, for an absolute constant C, that for every eps>0 and all sufficiently large t, t^4/(log t)^(3+eps) <= r(5,t) <= C t^4/(log t)^3, hence lim (4 log t - log r(5,t))/log log t = 3, i.e. r(5,t) = t^4/(log t)^(3+o(1)). The lower bound comes from a K_5-free graph on floor(q^4 log q) vertices with independence number below q(log q)^(1+eta), for prime q near t/(log t)^(1+eta) (Bertrand's postulate). The graph's vertices are positions in a random stream of ordered point-hyperplane flags (a in PG(4,q), b a hyperplane containing a), with an edge for i<j when a_i lies on b_j but a_j does not lie on b_i; the existence of a stream with no long consistent subsequence is shown by an entropy/compression contradiction. The upper bound is an elementary sampling argument (uniform independent sets, triangle-free independence bound, random sampling and deletion), giving r(5,t) <= C t^4/(log t)^3. (2) 'Sharp Logarithmic Exponents for Fixed Off-Diagonal Ramsey Numbers' (main.tex, dated 24 September 2026) claims, for each fixed s >= 6 and constant C_s, that for every eps>0 and all sufficiently large t, t^(s-1)/(log t)^(s-2+eps) <= r(s,t) <= C_s t^(s-1)/(log t)^(s-2), hence lim ((s-1) log t - log r(s,t))/log log t = s-2. It runs the same method in PG(d,q) with d = s-1 >= 5, producing K_(d+1)-free graphs on floor(q^d log q) vertices with independence number below q(log q)^(1+eta) (Theorem intro:prime-construction, proved via the entropy contradiction in end:section), and derives the upper bound by induction on s (Proposition end:upper-bound, stated for every s >= 2). Together the two manuscripts cover every fixed s >= 5.
entries.delivers: Asymptotic information only, for the family r(s,t) with s fixed (s >= 5) and t -> infinity: the logarithmic exponent of r(s,t) is s-2 over t^(s-1), i.e. r(s,t) = t^(s-1)/(log t)^(s-2+o(1)). This is a statement about the order of magnitude of one row of the two-colour table, in the off-diagonal regime. It does not determine the value of any R(r,s), and it gives no numerical bound on any specific value: the constants are unspecified (absolute C and C_s), and the lower bound carries (log t)^eps slack that absorbs constants. Neither manuscript mentions the diagonal number R(5,5) or any diagonal value, and the asymptotic regime (s fixed, t large) does not reach R(5,5). The manuscripts do not claim to determine the values of the Ramsey numbers. Paper 2 explicitly says its theorem 'does not assert that r(s,t) is bounded below by a positive constant times t^(s-1)/(log t)^(s-2)'. Neither manuscript restates the list's problem; both state an asymptotic exponent for r(s,t), which is a different question from determining the values. These results are progress only in the bound sense the matching pass recorded.
entries.remains: If the claims are correct, still open for this problem: (a) the exact value of R(5,5), and the values of R(r,s) generally; the problem's own statement gives 43 <= R(5,5) <= 46, which neither manuscript changes; (b) for R(s,t) with s fixed, the constant-factor asymptotic: paper 1 says it 'leaves open a constant-factor asymptotic for t^4/(log t)^3', and paper 2 leaves open whether r(s,t) is bounded below by c_s t^(s-1)/(log t)^(s-2); (c) any explicit (non-probabilistic) lower-bound construction, since the lower-bound graphs are shown to exist by a contradiction argument; (d) all regimes other than s fixed with t -> infinity, including the diagonal case and the multicolour, hypergraph and graph-Ramsey readings of the bare phrase 'the Ramsey numbers'.
entries.direction: determines the logarithmic exponent of R(s,t) for fixed s >= 5 as t grows (asymptotic order, not values); proves an asymptotic bound, not a value
entries.object: The lower-bound objects are graphs with no K_s (K_5 in paper 1, K_(d+1) in paper 2) and independence number below about q(log q)^(1+eta) on about q^d log q vertices, for prime q. They are shown to exist by an entropy contradiction (some stream of flags has no consistent subsequence of length k), not constructed explicitly. Null for any specific Ramsey number value.
entries.conditional_on: No unproven hypothesis is assumed; both results are claimed unconditional. Dependencies on other sources: paper 2's construction is an ordered version of Bradac's incident-flag graph (arXiv:2605.28793, Section 2.5), and its marking argument adapts Bradac's Claim 2.13 and Lemma 2.12; paper 2 also cites the companion paper 'The Sharp Logarithmic Exponent of r(5,t)' (Lemma 3.4, Theorem 4.1) for the selected-law entropy and low-dimensional sparse-pair framework, and states that 'the present paper supplies all the required arguments locally'. Paper 2's rich-subspace bound is said to be a consequence of Nie and Wang's finite-degree closure inequality (Theorems 4.1 and 5.6), though a self-contained evaluation-rank proof is given. Paper 1 relies on Bradac's Lemma 2.1 and Claim 2.13, on Kollar's Theorem 2 (predictor-geometry), and on Dvir, Guth-Katz, Elekes-Kaplan-Sharir and Ellenberg-Hablicsek for polynomial estimates, all cited as external inputs. Paper 2's theorem is not derived from paper 1's theorem; it depends on paper 1 only through the framework it cites.
entries.doubts: Paper 1: the lower bound rests on the stream theorem (compression-tree.tex, thm:stream) and the sparse-pair description theorem (predictor-statement.tex, thm:predictor). The proof of the compression stage (prop:compression-stage) is a short paragraph that assembles lemmas from other files (lem:marking, lem:decoupling, lem:high-ranks, lem:flat-levels, lem:pivot-retention, lem:pivot-compression), and the text does not label any step as sketched or conditional. The lower bound is only as strong as that chain. The theorem's constants are absolute, and the limit statement is equivalent to the stated two-sided bound. Paper 2: the text cites the companion paper for the s = 5 framework that it adapts to d >= 5, and also says the present paper supplies all the required arguments locally; the text does not say precisely which companion results are carried over versus re-proved. The uniformity of constants across the T+1 compression stages is argued by a recursive prescription (06-conclusion, the paragraph beginning 'The constants and thresholds can be fixed without knowing the actual conditional laws') rather than by explicit computation. Both manuscripts hold their statements for sufficiently large q or t with thresholds not made explicit.
